## Intent
Hypothesis: sequential identity-ordering allows scalar per-particle processing to approach the streaming ceiling despite branchy respawn.

## Cache saturation
All tested N (10000–10000000) exceed the L2 spill at N≈7710; N=10000 and N=100000 fit in L3 (16 MB), while N≥1000000 spills to DRAM. The ns/particle curve is FLAT across N at every death rate: q=0.01 ranges 25.42–26.69 ns/p, q=0.5 ranges 34.64–34.886 ns/p. No knee appears at the L3→DRAM transition — cost rises only ~1 ns/p between N=100000 and N=1000000. Death rate raises the floor monotonically (q=0.01→~25.5, q=0.1→~27.3, q=0.25→~30, q=0.5→~34.8 ns/p) without altering the N-shape. The evidence is silent on behavior below the L2 spill since the smallest tested N is 10000.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 2.68 GB/s at N=10000, q=0.01 — 21% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. Bandwidth stays flat across all N and death rates (2.25–2.68 GB/s), never approaching the ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: perf attributes 63.8–70.2% of cycles to frontend stalls and only 29.8–36.1% to compute, with 0.0% backend stalls throughout. No transition occurs by N or death rate — the algo is uniformly frontend-limited.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize: the histogram shows 0 vector-suffixed instructions. All floating-point work uses scalar `vmovss` (32), `vmulss` (13), `vaddss` (11), and `vucomiss` (11) — one component at a time per particle, no gather. Branchy respawn appears as `call` to `spawn` and `Random.fill`, with `lzcnt` (3) for RNG and `div` (1) for index wraparound. Byte-granular scatter stores (`mov BYTE PTR [r13+r14*1+0x0],dl`) with `cmovae` (12) clamping to 0xff confirm the de-vec control flow. This scalar codegen with per-particle branching explains the 63.8–70.2% frontend stalls and 21% bandwidth utilization — the core cannot retire instructions fast enough to saturate memory.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo achieves only 2.68 GB/s (21% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, with 0 vectorized instructions and 63.8–70.2% frontend stalls across all regimes. Sequential ordering cannot compensate for scalar per-particle processing with branchy respawn; the algo is uniformly frontend-bound, and death rate merely raises the floor (25.42→34.64 ns/p at N=10000 from q=0.01 to q=0.5) without changing the N-scaling shape.
